subject: Storix POC kickoff & benchmark runbook — scheduling and pre-checks
messages:
From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@storix.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@storix.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Storix POC kickoff — proposed goals and timing

Hi Diego / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Storix is ready to move to an official POC (hands-on) so we can validate throughput and tail latency with a realistic prompt set and routing rules. High-level asks from our end: 

- Throughput target: sustained 50 requests/sec for the primary route, spike to 100rps for short bursts (2–5m)
- Latency SLO: 95p < 120ms, 99p < 250ms for the single-token/streaming scenario
- Test harness: we’ll provide a JMeter script + sample dataset (~30k prompt pairs) but we need to align on auth/token rotation and KV cache warmup
- Runbook review: validate what Redwood will instrument and what Storix needs to collect (traces, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route QPS)

Can we schedule a 90-minute hands-on kickoff next week to: review the runbook, slot the load windows, and run a light canary? Ideally the week of July 6 — we can be flexible with time zones (Storix team is PST).

I attached our high-level requirements (storix-requirements-v2.xlsx). Let me know availability and if you prefer we run the canary the day before the main run.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Jacobs
Head of Platform Engineering, Storix AI
[Attachment: storix-requirements-v2.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB)]

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@storix.ai>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@storix.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storix POC kickoff — proposed goals and timing

Ben —

Appreciate the clear goals. We’re excited to run this with you. Quick notes and asks before we lock a slot: 

- Redwood can meet the throughput/latency targets you listed; we’ll bring a dedicated orchestration slot and reserve capacity for the main run.
- Can you confirm the sample dataset size (rows) you plan to use for the 50rps steady-state? Also whether prompts include streaming responses or single-shot generation.
- Please confirm which AWS region you want the runs in (we suggest us-west-2 to match your PST team).

Proposed slots (90 minutes) — Pacific time: 
- Tue Jul 7, 08:00–09:30
- Wed Jul 8, 10:00–11:30
- Thu Jul 9, 07:30–09:00

We’ll attach our POC runbook (redwood-poc-runbook.pdf) with the checklist (pre-warm, sample sizes, metric hooks, and test-harness instructions). If you prefer a short canary the day before, we can reserve a 45-minute window on Mon Jul 6 evening (PST).

Marissa will be the lead on day-of. Karthik will own the test harness and load config.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-runbook.pdf (pdf, 1.4MB)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@storix.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@storix.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storix POC kickoff — proposed goals and timing

Thanks — a few technical clarifications from the test-harness side: 

- Auth / tokens: The harness should rotate short-lived tokens every 15 minutes. I’ll publish a small helper script to mint and attach tokens to the JMeter threads.
- Warm-up: We should do a 15–20 minute KV cache warm-up at ~10% load prior to the canary to get stable latencies; otherwise first-run cold KV will inflate the 99p.
- Payload sizing: For 50rps steady-state we recommend a 25k–35k prompt sample with avg token length ~120 tokens. Please indicate if your sample is larger.
- Measurement hooks: We’ll record per-token timing, model-level stats (kv hit/miss), and open telemetry traces. Can you share the JMeter script and one sample prompt set ahead of the run?

Operational windows I prefer (PST): 
- Wed Jul 8, 10:00–11:30 (matches Diego slot) — good for engineering overlap
- Thu Jul 9, 07:30–09:00 — ok but lighter on Storix’s product PMs

I’ll also include the load configuration we plan to run (steady 50rps, 5m spikes to 100rps, 30s ramp).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Performance & Serving, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@storix.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@storix.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storix POC kickoff — proposed goals and timing

Diego / Karthik —

Thanks — Wed Jul 8 at 10:00 PST works best for us. One request: can we move the canary to Mon Jul 6 at 18:00 PST instead of Jul 7? We have a stakeholder review on Jul 7 afternoon and would like the canary results earlier. If you need to reschedule any internal prep, let us know.

I attached a slightly updated requirements sheet (minor clarifications on streaming vs single-shot for two prompt families). We’ll upload the JMeter script and a 30k sample prompt set to the Drive link by EOD tomorrow.

Also: for the canary we only need a 30-minute run (low load) to validate routing and token rotation. The 90-minute Wed session will be the full benchmark.

Cheers,
Ben
[Attachment: storix-requirements-v2.xlsx (updated, xlsx, 235KB)]

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@storix.ai>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@storix.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Storix POC kickoff — confirmed: canary + benchmark slots

Ben —

All set. Confirming updated schedule and agenda below: 

Confirmed slots (PST):
- Canary: Mon Jul 6, 18:00–18:30 (30 minutes) — quick routing/auth smoke + low-load validation
- Full benchmark & runbook walkthrough: Wed Jul 8, 10:00–11:30 (90 minutes) — warm-up, steady-state run, manual spike windows, and post-run analysis

Agenda (Wed Jul 8, 10:00 PST) — 90m
1) 10:00–10:10: Introductions & goals (Diego)
2) 10:10–10:25: Runbook review and measurement hooks (Marissa)
3) 10:25–10:45: Canary recap and warm-up plan (Karthik)
4) 10:45–11:15: Steady-state 50rps + two 5m spike windows to 100rps
5) 11:15–11:25: Quick data snapshot + tracing review
6) 11:25–11:30: Next steps and rollout plan

Logistics: Zoom link: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/9876543210
Drive (upload folder): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cRedwoodRunbook
HubSpot record: HS-52380

Please confirm who will be on the call from Storix. We’ll prepare a short results dashboard and export the per-token traces for your team.

—Diego
